fields.features_heading: What a Rental Agreement Form Should Cover
fields.features_subheading: Every agreement rests on the same core terms. Emergent turns them into fields and keeps track of each lease once it is signed.
fields.feature_1:
Every term in its own field

Emergent asks for the parties, the address, the lease term, the rent with its due date and grace period, the late fee, the deposit, utilities, pets and who handles repairs.
fields.feature_2:
Your terms fixed, their details asked

Set the rent and house rules before the link goes out. Tenants fill in only their own part, starting with the legal name of every adult who will live there and a move-in date.
fields.feature_3:
A filled agreement ready to sign

Submitting the form produces the agreement as a PDF with every blank completed. Each party signs on screen, and the signed copy is emailed to everyone and stored with that lease.
fields.feature_4:
The right disclosures on each lease

Record when each property was built, and units from before 1978 get the lead paint disclosure and EPA pamphlet in their packet. Attach state or city addenda by property too.
fields.feature_5:
One table for every lease you manage

Each signed agreement becomes a row with its unit, tenants, rent and end date. Sort the table by end date or filter it by property, and get an email before any lease runs out.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your source code

Publish the form on your own domain or link it from a rental listing. Export the full source to GitHub whenever a developer wants to add a tenant portal or online rent collection.

fields.usecase_heading: Rental Agreement Forms for Every Property
fields.tab_content_1:
House rules the tenant signs before move-in

One link goes to the new tenant of a spare room. They enter a move-in date and an emergency contact, then read the house rules: quiet after 10 pm, overnight guests for 3 nights at most. Rent is $950, due on the 1st. The agreement goes out for signature the moment they submit.
fields.tab_content_2:
Leases ending within 60 days surface first

Every lease at Birch Court sits in one table, sorted by end date. Anything ending within 60 days rises to the top, and the property manager gets an email to start the renewal conversation. All 48 units stay in one view instead of a folder of PDFs.
fields.tab_content_3:
Nothing is final until the last roommate signs

Each roommate on the lease gets a personal signing link and sees their share: $800 of the $2,400 rent. The landlord can see who has signed. Anyone still unsigned after two days gets a reminder, and the finished copy reaches all three once the last signature is in.
fields.tab_content_4:
Collect the damage deposit with the booking

Guests booking the lake house accept the stay rules on the same form they book with: check-in at 4 pm, checkout by 11 am, six guests at most. A $300 damage deposit is collected through Stripe, and the stay is confirmed only after the guest signs.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Rental Agreement Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the terms before you write a single field. Seven steps take you from that list to a published form that sends every agreement out for signature.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the terms that never change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide what the tenant fills in
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what stays the same for every tenant at this property: rent, due date, grace period, late fee, deposit, utilities, pets and repair duties. These become fixed text in the agreement, and no tenant can edit them when they fill in the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only for what changes from one tenant to the next. Names of the adults on the lease and the move-in date are the core; add other occupants or vehicles if your rules depend on them. Keep income and background questions for a separate screening step.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Deposit limits and required disclosures vary by state. California, for example, caps most deposits at one month's rent and gives landlords 21 days after move-out to return them. Federal rules add a lead paint disclosure for most housing built before 1978.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the property and paste your terms into the prompt. Emergent builds the form and the lease table that stores each signed copy. Change any wording later by asking in plain English, and the update goes live on the same link.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose who signs and in what order. Tenants usually sign first and the landlord countersigns last. Once every signature is in, the app emails the signed PDF to each party and attaches it to that lease's row in the table.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add reminders for the lease term
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the moments that need a nudge, like an agreement still unsigned after two days or a lease close to its end date. Send each reminder by email or Slack to the person who acts on it, with a direct link to the record.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with a made-up tenant
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form as a fictional tenant, sign as both parties and read the PDF line by line. Then have a local attorney review the agreement text before the first real tenant signs it. Fix anything they flag by prompting, and test once more.

claims_to_source: A rental agreement states the rent, the due date, the grace period and any late fees, the security deposit terms, who pays each utility, the pet rules and repair duties
A month-to-month rental agreement renews with each rent payment, while a lease fixes the rent and terms for a set period, usually six months or a year
Landlords of most housing built before 1978 must disclose known lead-based paint and include a Lead Warning Statement; leases of 100 days or less are exempt
In California, a lease longer than one year must be in writing and signed
California limits most security deposits to one month's rent and requires the deposit back, with an itemized statement of deductions, within 21 days of move-out
